top_story: Iran’s threat to widen confrontation across the region dates back to March, when US pressure tied to the Strait of Hormuz prompted Tehran to signal that any attack on its infrastructure would trigger escalation beyond its borders. That warning now carries sharper operational significance after a US intelligence assessment on 24 October said Iranian efforts to target American personnel have intensified and some lethal plots are at advanced stages, raising the risk that deterrent messaging is shifting into covert action. In Sudan, the human cost of regionalized conflict is starkly visible in El-Fasher, where one year after the UAE-backed RSF seized the city, the population has collapsed to roughly seven percent of last year’s peak amid killings, torture, and disappearances. Together, these developments point to a Middle East and adjacent Red Sea arena where coercive state rivalry and proxy warfare are deepening insecurity for both civilians and foreign personnel.
